17	# LaTeX 论文写作全流程
18	
19	ML/AI 顶会论文从草稿到投稿的完整指南。整合 Orchestra Research、VibeSkills、claim2evidence 三方最佳实践。
20	
21	---
22	
23	## 1. 工作模式
24	
25	开始前选择模式：
26	
27	| 模式 | 说明 | 适用 |
28	|------|------|------|
29	| **Build** | 从实验笔记/结果/代码生成论文 | 新稿 |
30	| **Improve** | 改写已有章节，强化论证 | 修改稿 |
31	| **Audit** | 输出风险列表 + 缺失证据 + 修复建议 | 投前检查 |
32	
33	---
34	
35	## 2. Claim-Evidence 方法论
36	
37	**核心原则：论文是一个有中心贡献的故事，不是实验的堆砌。**
38	
39	### 2.1 一句话贡献
40	
41	在写任何内容之前，必须能用一句话说清贡献。如果不能，说明还没准备好写论文。
42	
43	### 2.2 Claim-Evidence Map
44	
45	为每个 contribution 建立 claim→evidence 映射表：
46	
47	| Contribution | Claim | Evidence | Table/Figure |
48	|-------------|-------|----------|-------------|
49	| C1: 方法 X 在 Y 上 SOTA | 比所有 baseline 高 ≥2% | 5-seed 平均，p<0.05 | Table 1 |
50	| C2: 消融证明 Z 是关键 | 去掉 Z 后掉 >5% | 消融实验 | Table 2 |
51	| C3: 计算效率 | 比 baseline 快 3× | FLOPs + wall-clock | Figure 3 |
52	
53	**没有直接证据支撑的 claim 必须删除或降级为 discussion。**
54	
55	### 2.3 章节起草顺序
56	
57	```
58	1. Introduction + Experiments（先确定 claim 和 evidence）
59	2. Method（评估问题稳定后再写细节）
60	3. Related Work
61	4. Abstract + Title（核心 claim 定型后最后写）
62	```
63	
64	### 2.4 Quality Gates
65	
66	投稿前必须通过：
67	- [ ] 前两段出现显式 novelty 声明
68	- [ ] 每个 contribution 有可验证的 evidence
69	- [ ] Abstract / Intro / Conclusion 的 claim 一致
70	- [ ] Limitations 真实且技术性诚实
71	- [ ] 审稿人两分钟内能识别 delta
72	
73	---
74	
75	## 3. 引用防幻觉（CRITICAL）
76	
77	**AI 生成引用有 ~40% 错误率。绝对禁止凭记忆写 BibTeX。**
78	
79	### 3.1 黄金法则
80	
81	```
82	IF 无法程序化获取引用:
83	    → 标记 [CITATION NEEDED] 或 \cite{PLACEHOLDER_verify}
84	    → 明确告知用户
85	    → 绝不编造看似合理的引用
86	```
87	
88	### 3.2 五步验证流程
89	
90	```
91	1. SEARCH  → Semantic Scholar API 搜索关键词
92	2. VERIFY  → 至少 2 个来源确认论文存在（S2 + arXiv/CrossRef）
93	3. RETRIEVE → 通过 DOI 获取 BibTeX（程序化，非记忆）
94	4. CHECK   → 确认你引用的 claim 确实出自该论文
95	5. ADD     → 加入 .bib 文件
96	```
97	
98	### 3.3 API 速查
99	
100	| API | 用途 | 限制 |
101	|-----|------|------|
102	| **Semantic Scholar** | ML/AI 论文搜索 | 1 RPS (免费) |
103	| **CrossRef** | DOI → BibTeX | 需 mailto 头 |
104	| **arXiv** | 预印本搜索 | 3s 间隔 |
105	
106	```python
107	# DOI → BibTeX（最可靠的方式）
108	import requests
109	def doi_to_bibtex(doi: str) -> str:
110	    r = requests.get(f"https://doi.org/{doi}",
111	                     headers={"Accept": "application/x-bibtex"})
112	    r.raise_for_status()
113	    return r.text
114	
115	# Semantic Scholar 搜索
116	from semanticscholar import SemanticScholar
117	sch = SemanticScholar()
118	results = sch.search_paper("attention mechanism transformers", limit=5)
119	for p in results:
120	    print(f"{p.title} | DOI: {p.externalIds.get('DOI', 'N/A')}")
121	```
122	
123	### 3.4 引用处理规则
124	
125	| 情况 | 处理 |
126	|------|------|
127	| 找到论文 + DOI + BibTeX | 直接用 |
128	| 找到论文，无 DOI | 用 arXiv BibTeX |
129	| 论文存在但无法获取 BibTeX | 标记 placeholder，告知用户 |
130	| 不确定论文是否存在 | 标记 `[CITATION NEEDED]`，告知用户 |
131	| "我觉得有篇关于 X 的论文" | **绝不引用** — 先搜索或标记 |
132	
133	---
134	
135	## 4. 顶会模板速查
136	
137	### 4.1 ML/AI 会议
138	
139	| 会议 | 页数限制 | 主文件 | 样式文件 | 必须项 |
140	|------|---------|--------|---------|--------|
141	| **NeurIPS** | 9 页 | `main.tex` | `neurips.sty` | Paper Checklist |
142	| **ICML** | 8 页 (+1 camera-ready) | `example_paper.tex` | `icml2026.sty` | Broader Impact |
143	| **ICLR** | 9 页 (+1) | `iclr_conference.tex` | `iclr_conference.sty` | LLM 使用声明 |
144	| **ACL/EMNLP** | 8 页 (long) | `acl_latex.tex` | `acl.sty` | Limitations 必须 |
145	| **AAAI** | 7 页 (+1) | `aaai_template.tex` | `aaai.sty` | 严格样式 |
146	| **COLM** | 9 页 (+1) | `colm_conference.tex` | `colm_conference.sty` | 语言模型聚焦 |
147	
148	### 4.2 系统会议
149	
150	| 会议 | 页数限制 | 模板类型 | 关键要求 |
151	|------|---------|---------|---------|
152	| **OSDI** | 12 页 (+2) | USENIX `usenix.sty` | Research / Operational 双 track |
153	| **NSDI** | 12 页 | USENIX | Introduction 预筛 |
154	| **ASPLOS** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 前 2 页快速评审 |
155	| **SOSP** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 可选 Artifact Evaluation |
156	
157	### 4.3 模板使用原则
158	
159	```bash
160	# 1. 复制整个模板目录（不要只拷 .tex）
161	cp -r templates/neurips2025/ ~/papers/my-paper/
162	
163	# 2. 先编译未修改的模板，确认能跑通
164	latexmk -pdf main.tex
165	
166	# 3. 逐章替换内容，频繁编译
167	```
168	
169	**禁止事项：**
170	- 不要修改 `.sty` 文件
171	- 不要在会议模板间复制 `\usepackage` 行
172	- 不要只复制 `.tex` 而不带 `.sty/.bst`
173	
174	---
175	
176	## 5. 写作规范
177	
178	### 5.1 时间分配（Neel Nanda）
179	
180	花**大致相等**的时间在：
181	1. Abstract
182	2. Introduction
183	3. 图表
184	4. **其余所有内容加起来**
185	
186	审稿人读论文的顺序：标题 → 摘要 → 引言 → 图表 → 也许正文。
187	
188	### 5.2 Abstract 五句法（Sebastian Farquhar）
189	
190	```
191	1. 你做了什么（"We introduce/prove/demonstrate..."）
192	2. 为什么这很难且重要
193	3. 怎么做的（含专业关键词以便检索）
194	4. 有什么证据
195	5. 最惊人的数字/结果
196	```
197	
198	删除一切泛泛的开头：~~"Large language models have achieved remarkable success..."~~
199	
200	### 5.3 句子级清晰度（Gopen & Swan）
201	
202	| 原则 | 规则 |
203	|------|------|
204	| 主谓紧邻 | 不要在主语和动词之间插入长从句 |
205	| 重点在句尾 | 把关键数字/结论放在句末 |
206	| 旧信息在前 | 先放读者已知的内容，再引入新概念 |
207	| 动词表达动作 | "We analyzed" 而非 "We performed an analysis" |
208	
209	### 5.4 常见修改
210	
211	| 问题 | 修复 |
212	|------|------|
213	| Abstract 太泛 | 删第一句（如果它能放在任何 ML 论文前面） |
214	| Introduction 超 1.5 页 | 背景挪到 Related Work |
215	| 实验没有显式 claim | 每个实验前加 "This tests whether..." |
216	| 缺统计显著性 | 加 error bars + 运行次数 + 计算方法 |
217	
218	---
219	
220	## 6. 投稿工程链
221	
222	### 6.1 构建
223	
224	```bash
225	# 推荐：latexmk 一键构建
226	latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error main.tex
227	
228	# 手动：需要多次编译
229	pdflatex main.tex && bibtex main && pdflatex main.tex && pdflatex main.tex
230	```
231	
232	### 6.2 Lint + 格式化
233	
234	```bash
235	# Lint: 检查常见 LaTeX 问题
236	chktex main.tex
237	
238	# 格式化: 减少 diff 噪声
239	latexindent -w main.tex
240	```
241	
242	### 6.3 图表格式
243	
244	| 类型 | 格式 | 说明 |
245	|------|------|------|
246	| 矢量图（plot、diagram） | PDF | matplotlib: `plt.savefig('fig.pdf')` |
247	| 照片/heatmap | PNG 600dpi 或 TIFF | 栅格图 |
248	| 表格 | `booktabs` 包 | `\toprule/\midrule/\bottomrule` |
249	
250	```latex
251	\usepackage{booktabs}
252	\begin{tabular}{lcc}
253	\toprule
254	Method & Accuracy $\uparrow$ & Latency $\downarrow$ \\
255	\midrule
256	Baseline & 85.2 & 45ms \\
257	\textbf{Ours} & \textbf{92.1} & 38ms \\
258	\bottomrule
259	\end{tabular}
260	```
261	
262	**图表规范：**
263	- 用色盲友好色板（Okabe-Ito 或 Paul Tol）
264	- 图内不放标题（用 caption）
265	- Caption 独立可理解（不依赖正文）
266	- 最佳值加粗，标注方向符号（↑ 越高越好，↓ 越低越好）
267	
268	### 6.4 投稿打包
269	
270	```bash
271	# 清理辅助文件
272	latexmk -c
273	
274	# 打包投稿
275	zip -r submission.zip main.tex *.sty *.bst *.bib figures/ --exclude='*.aux' --exclude='*.log'
276	```
277	
278	### 6.5 常见失败点
279	
280	| 问题 | 解决 |
281	|------|------|
282	| 图片格式混用导致编译失败 | 统一用 PDF |
283	| 字体未嵌入 | `pdffonts output.pdf` 检查 |
284	| Overfull box 过多 | 关键位置手动调行 |
285	| 引用缺字段 | 检查 DOI/年份/期刊名 |
286	| 超页数 | 用 `\vspace{-Xpt}` 微调，或精简内容 |
287	
288	---
289	
290	## 7. 会议转投
291	
292	当论文被拒或转投其他会议时：
293	
294	### 7.1 ML/AI 会议间转换
295	
296	| 转换 | 页数变化 | 关键调整 |
297	|------|---------|---------|
298	| NeurIPS → ICML | 9→8 | 删 1 页，加 Broader Impact |
299	| ICML → ICLR | 8→9 | 可扩展实验 + LLM 声明 |
300	| NeurIPS → ACL | 9→8 | 按 NLP 惯例重组 + Limitations |
301	| ICLR → AAAI | 9→7 | 大幅精简，严格样式 |
302	
303	### 7.2 转投原则
304	
305	1. **永远用目标模板重新开始** — 复制目标模板，迁移内容，不要合并 preamble
306	2. **只迁移正文内容** — 不复制 `\usepackage`、header/footer 命令
307	3. **根据审稿意见改进** — 但不要在新稿中提及旧投稿（双盲）
308	4. **检查目标会议特殊要求** — checklist、ethics statement、LLM 声明等
309	
310	---
311	
312	## 8. 投前清单
313	
314	### 通用清单
315	
316	- [ ] Abstract/Intro/Conclusion 的 claim 一致
317	- [ ] 每个 contribution 有对应 evidence
318	- [ ] 所有引用已程序化验证（无幻觉引用）
319	- [ ] Error bars + 运行次数 + 统计方法
320	- [ ] Limitations 章节存在且诚实
321	- [ ] 匿名化（双盲审稿）
322	- [ ] 符合页数限制
323	- [ ] 所有图表有自包含 caption
324	- [ ] `.bib` 中无缺失字段
325	- [ ] PDF 编译无 warning
326	
327	### 会议特定
328	
329	| 会议 | 额外要求 |
330	|------|---------|
331	| NeurIPS | 16 项 Paper Checklist（附录，不计页数） |
332	| ICML | Broader Impact Statement |
333	| ICLR | LLM 使用声明 |
334	| ACL/EMNLP | Limitations 章节（必须），Ethics Statement |
335	| AAAI | 严格样式文件合规 |
336	
337	---
338	
339	## 参考资源
340	
341	**写作方法论：**
342	- [Neel Nanda: How to Write ML Papers](https://www.alignmentforum.org/posts/eJGptPbbFPZGLpjsp/) — What/Why/So What 框架
343	- [Farquhar: How to Write ML Papers](https://sebastianfarquhar.com/on-research/2024/11/04/how_to_write_ml_papers/) — 五句法 Abstract
344	- [Gopen & Swan: Science of Scientific Writing](https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~swanson/papers/science-of-writing.pdf) — 读者预期 7 原则
345	- [Lipton: Heuristics for Scientific Writing](https://www.approximatelycorrect.com/2018/01/29/heuristics-technical-scientific-writing-machine-learning-perspective/) — 用词
346	- [Perez: Easy Paper Writing Tips](https://ethanperez.net/easy-paper-writing-tips/) — 微观清晰度
347	
348	**API：**
349	- [Semantic Scholar](https://api.semanticscholar.org/api-docs/) | [CrossRef](https://www.crossref.org/documentation/) | [arXiv](https://info.arxiv.org/help/api/)
350	
351	**会议官方：**
352	- [NeurIPS](https://neurips.cc/) | [ICML](https://icml.cc/) | [ICLR](https://iclr.cc/) | [ACL](https://www.aclweb.org/) | [AAAI](https://aaai.org/) | [EMNLP](https://2025.emnlp.org/)

# LaTeX 论文写作全流程

ML/AI 顶会论文从草稿到投稿的完整指南。整合 Orchestra Research、VibeSkills、claim2evidence 三方最佳实践。

---

## 1. 工作模式

开始前选择模式：

| 模式 | 说明 | 适用 |
|------|------|------|
| **Build** | 从实验笔记/结果/代码生成论文 | 新稿 |
| **Improve** | 改写已有章节，强化论证 | 修改稿 |
| **Audit** | 输出风险列表 + 缺失证据 + 修复建议 | 投前检查 |

---

## 2. Claim-Evidence 方法论

**核心原则：论文是一个有中心贡献的故事，不是实验的堆砌。**

### 2.1 一句话贡献

在写任何内容之前，必须能用一句话说清贡献。如果不能，说明还没准备好写论文。

### 2.2 Claim-Evidence Map

为每个 contribution 建立 claim→evidence 映射表：

| Contribution | Claim | Evidence | Table/Figure |
|-------------|-------|----------|-------------|
| C1: 方法 X 在 Y 上 SOTA | 比所有 baseline 高 ≥2% | 5-seed 平均，p<0.05 | Table 1 |
| C2: 消融证明 Z 是关键 | 去掉 Z 后掉 >5% | 消融实验 | Table 2 |
| C3: 计算效率 | 比 baseline 快 3× | FLOPs + wall-clock | Figure 3 |

**没有直接证据支撑的 claim 必须删除或降级为 discussion。**

### 2.3 章节起草顺序

```
1. Introduction + Experiments（先确定 claim 和 evidence）
2. Method（评估问题稳定后再写细节）
3. Related Work
4. Abstract + Title（核心 claim 定型后最后写）
```

### 2.4 Quality Gates

投稿前必须通过：
- [ ] 前两段出现显式 novelty 声明
- [ ] 每个 contribution 有可验证的 evidence
- [ ] Abstract / Intro / Conclusion 的 claim 一致
- [ ] Limitations 真实且技术性诚实
- [ ] 审稿人两分钟内能识别 delta

---

## 3. 引用防幻觉（CRITICAL）

**AI 生成引用有 ~40% 错误率。绝对禁止凭记忆写 BibTeX。**

### 3.1 黄金法则

```
IF 无法程序化获取引用:
    → 标记 [CITATION NEEDED] 或 \cite{PLACEHOLDER_verify}
    → 明确告知用户
    → 绝不编造看似合理的引用
```

### 3.2 五步验证流程

```
1. SEARCH  → Semantic Scholar API 搜索关键词
2. VERIFY  → 至少 2 个来源确认论文存在（S2 + arXiv/CrossRef）
3. RETRIEVE → 通过 DOI 获取 BibTeX（程序化，非记忆）
4. CHECK   → 确认你引用的 claim 确实出自该论文
5. ADD     → 加入 .bib 文件
```

### 3.3 API 速查

| API | 用途 | 限制 |
|-----|------|------|
| **Semantic Scholar** | ML/AI 论文搜索 | 1 RPS (免费) |
| **CrossRef** | DOI → BibTeX | 需 mailto 头 |
| **arXiv** | 预印本搜索 | 3s 间隔 |

```python
# DOI → BibTeX（最可靠的方式）
import requests
def doi_to_bibtex(doi: str) -> str:
    r = requests.get(f"https://doi.org/{doi}",
                     headers={"Accept": "application/x-bibtex"})
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.text

# Semantic Scholar 搜索
from semanticscholar import SemanticScholar
sch = SemanticScholar()
results = sch.search_paper("attention mechanism transformers", limit=5)
for p in results:
    print(f"{p.title} | DOI: {p.externalIds.get('DOI', 'N/A')}")
```

### 3.4 引用处理规则

| 情况 | 处理 |
|------|------|
| 找到论文 + DOI + BibTeX | 直接用 |
| 找到论文，无 DOI | 用 arXiv BibTeX |
| 论文存在但无法获取 BibTeX | 标记 placeholder，告知用户 |
| 不确定论文是否存在 | 标记 `[CITATION NEEDED]`，告知用户 |
| "我觉得有篇关于 X 的论文" | **绝不引用** — 先搜索或标记 |

---

## 4. 顶会模板速查

### 4.1 ML/AI 会议

| 会议 | 页数限制 | 主文件 | 样式文件 | 必须项 |
|------|---------|--------|---------|--------|
| **NeurIPS** | 9 页 | `main.tex` | `neurips.sty` | Paper Checklist |
| **ICML** | 8 页 (+1 camera-ready) | `example_paper.tex` | `icml2026.sty` | Broader Impact |
| **ICLR** | 9 页 (+1) | `iclr_conference.tex` | `iclr_conference.sty` | LLM 使用声明 |
| **ACL/EMNLP** | 8 页 (long) | `acl_latex.tex` | `acl.sty` | Limitations 必须 |
| **AAAI** | 7 页 (+1) | `aaai_template.tex` | `aaai.sty` | 严格样式 |
| **COLM** | 9 页 (+1) | `colm_conference.tex` | `colm_conference.sty` | 语言模型聚焦 |

### 4.2 系统会议

| 会议 | 页数限制 | 模板类型 | 关键要求 |
|------|---------|---------|---------|
| **OSDI** | 12 页 (+2) | USENIX `usenix.sty` | Research / Operational 双 track |
| **NSDI** | 12 页 | USENIX | Introduction 预筛 |
| **ASPLOS** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 前 2 页快速评审 |
| **SOSP** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 可选 Artifact Evaluation |

### 4.3 模板使用原则

```bash
# 1. 复制整个模板目录（不要只拷 .tex）

# 2. 先编译未修改的模板，确认能跑通
latexmk -pdf main.tex

# 3. 逐章替换内容，频繁编译
```

**禁止事项：**
- 不要修改 `.sty` 文件
- 不要在会议模板间复制 `\usepackage` 行
- 不要只复制 `.tex` 而不带 `.sty/.bst`

---

## 5. 写作规范

### 5.1 时间分配（Neel Nanda）

花**大致相等**的时间在：
1. Abstract
2. Introduction
3. 图表
4. **其余所有内容加起来**

审稿人读论文的顺序：标题 → 摘要 → 引言 → 图表 → 也许正文。

### 5.2 Abstract 五句法（Sebastian Farquhar）

```
1. 你做了什么（"We introduce/prove/demonstrate..."）
2. 为什么这很难且重要
3. 怎么做的（含专业关键词以便检索）
4. 有什么证据
5. 最惊人的数字/结果
```

删除一切泛泛的开头：~~"Large language models have achieved remarkable success..."~~

### 5.3 句子级清晰度（Gopen & Swan）

| 原则 | 规则 |
|------|------|
| 主谓紧邻 | 不要在主语和动词之间插入长从句 |
| 重点在句尾 | 把关键数字/结论放在句末 |
| 旧信息在前 | 先放读者已知的内容，再引入新概念 |
| 动词表达动作 | "We analyzed" 而非 "We performed an analysis" |

### 5.4 常见修改

| 问题 | 修复 |
|------|------|
| Abstract 太泛 | 删第一句（如果它能放在任何 ML 论文前面） |
| Introduction 超 1.5 页 | 背景挪到 Related Work |
| 实验没有显式 claim | 每个实验前加 "This tests whether..." |
| 缺统计显著性 | 加 error bars + 运行次数 + 计算方法 |

---

## 6. 投稿工程链

### 6.1 构建

```bash
# 推荐：latexmk 一键构建
latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error main.tex

# 手动：需要多次编译
pdflatex main.tex && bibtex main && pdflatex main.tex && pdflatex main.tex
```

### 6.2 Lint + 格式化

```bash
# Lint: 检查常见 LaTeX 问题
chktex main.tex

# 格式化: 减少 diff 噪声
latexindent -w main.tex
```

### 6.3 图表格式

| 类型 | 格式 | 说明 |
|------|------|------|
| 矢量图（plot、diagram） | PDF | matplotlib: `plt.savefig('fig.pdf')` |
| 照片/heatmap | PNG 600dpi 或 TIFF | 栅格图 |
| 表格 | `booktabs` 包 | `\toprule/\midrule/\bottomrule` |

```latex

\begin{tabular}{lcc}
\toprule
Method & Accuracy $\uparrow$ & Latency $\downarrow$ \\
\midrule
Baseline & 85.2 & 45ms \\
\textbf{Ours} & \textbf{92.1} & 38ms \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
```

**图表规范：**
- 用色盲友好色板（Okabe-Ito 或 Paul Tol）
- 图内不放标题（用 caption）
- Caption 独立可理解（不依赖正文）
- 最佳值加粗，标注方向符号（↑ 越高越好，↓ 越低越好）

### 6.4 投稿打包

```bash
# 清理辅助文件
latexmk -c

# 打包投稿
zip -r submission.zip main.tex *.sty *.bst *.bib figures/ --exclude='*.aux' --exclude='*.log'
```

### 6.5 常见失败点

| 问题 | 解决 |
|------|------|
| 图片格式混用导致编译失败 | 统一用 PDF |
| 字体未嵌入 | `pdffonts output.pdf` 检查 |
| Overfull box 过多 | 关键位置手动调行 |
| 引用缺字段 | 检查 DOI/年份/期刊名 |
| 超页数 | 用 `\vspace{-Xpt}` 微调，或精简内容 |

## 7. 会议转投

当论文被拒或转投其他会议时：

# Introduction — Draft v1

\section{Introduction}

When LLM agents interact with rule-governed environments---manipulating temperatures, mixing chemicals, navigating physical constraints---they face a failure mode qualitatively distinct from suboptimality: \emph{catastrophic death}. A single hallucinated state transition can trigger an irreversible termination penalty, collapsing the episode score to $-100$. Deterministic external computation---environment simulators or code interpreters---eliminates such hallucinations by providing exact state transitions. But what does a router actually learn when trained to select between internal LLM reasoning and deterministic computation? Recent work on tool-use learning \cite{toolformer-2024,art-2023,chameleon-2024,retool-2026} and adaptive computation \cite{cogrouter-2026,ares-2026,mixture-of-recursions-2025} has developed methods for deciding when and how to invoke external modules, yet these approaches frame routing as a general capability or efficiency question---selecting the right tool, calibrating reasoning depth---without examining whether \emph{failure avoidance} constitutes a distinct and potentially dominant routing signal.

We address this question by analyzing routing between internal reasoning, following the ReAct interleaved reasoning-and-acting paradigm \cite{react-2023}, and deterministic computation on ScienceWorld, an interactive science environment with sparse rewards and catastrophic failure penalties. A natural first approach is per-step oracle comparison: at each decision point, run both modalities and prefer the one yielding higher immediate reward. However, in sparse-reward environments where non-zero reward arrives only at episode termination, this strategy degenerates. On ScienceWorld, per-step oracle labeling produces \textbf{[PLACEHOLDER: 98\%]} ties---neither modality shows a per-step advantage on the vast majority of steps---rendering the resulting labels uninformative for router training. This \emph{oracle degeneracy} motivates a shift from step-level to episode-level analysis.

We introduce \emph{episode-level counterfactual analysis}: for each task instance, we run complete episodes under pure-internal and pure-deterministic strategies, then compare episode-level outcomes to generate routing labels. Across [PLACEHOLDER: 30] ScienceWorld task types ([PLACEHOLDER: 249] episodes), this methodology reveals a striking concentration of routing signal. The full performance gap between deterministic and internal-reasoning strategies is [PLACEHOLDER: $\Delta_{\text{full}} = +37.9$] points. When we exclude episodes where either strategy results in agent death and recompute the gap, it collapses to [PLACEHOLDER: $\Delta_{\text{no\_death}} = +0.2$]---effectively zero. Death avoidance accounts for [PLACEHOLDER: 99\%] of the routing signal (death avoidance fraction [PLACEHOLDER: 98.75\%]). The per-task correlation between death rate differential and performance gap is $r =$ [PLACEHOLDER: 0.989] ($p < 0.0001$). Episode-level label distribution confirms this asymmetry: [PLACEHOLDER: 41\%] of episodes prefer deterministic computation, only [PLACEHOLDER: 0.5\%] prefer internal reasoning, and [PLACEHOLDER: 59\%] show no preference. When agents do not die, both reasoning modalities perform approximately equally.

Our contributions are:
\begin{itemize}
    \item We propose \textbf{episode-level counterfactual analysis} for routing label generation, overcoming the degeneracy of per-step oracle labeling in sparse-reward interactive environments (per-step tie rate of [PLACEHOLDER: 98\%] on ScienceWorld).
    \item We introduce a \textbf{death decomposition framework} that separates routing signal into death-avoidance and non-death components, quantifying how much routing value derives from catastrophic failure prevention versus positive task guidance.
    \item We provide \textbf{empirical evidence} across [PLACEHOLDER: 30] ScienceWorld task types that death avoidance accounts for [PLACEHOLDER: 99\%] of routing signal between internal LLM reasoning and deterministic computation, with non-death performance near-equivalent between modalities ([PLACEHOLDER: $\Delta_{\text{no\_death}} = +0.2$]).
\end{itemize}

# EMNLP 2026 Short Paper Outline

## Title Candidates

1. **Death Avoidance Dominates Routing Signal: A Counterfactual Analysis of LLM Agent Tool Use in Interactive Environments**
2. **When Does Deterministic Computation Help LLM Agents? Episode-Level Counterfactual Analysis Reveals Death Avoidance Dominance**
3. **90% Death Avoidance: Decomposing the Routing Signal Between LLM Reasoning and Deterministic Simulation**

Recommended: **Title 1** (clear claim + methodology in title; fits short paper convention of stating the finding)

---

## Abstract Skeleton (~150 words)

Key points to cover:

- **Problem**: LLM agents hallucinate state transitions in rule-governed environments, causing catastrophic failures (deaths). Routing between internal LLM reasoning and deterministic computation (simulators) can mitigate this, but what exactly does routing learn?
- **Methodological gap**: Per-step oracle labeling degenerates in sparse-reward settings (98% tie rate on ScienceWorld). We propose episode-level counterfactual analysis.
- **Core finding**: Death avoidance accounts for ~90% of routing signal (Δ_full=+29.60, Δ_no_death=+2.84, DAF=90.41%; Pearson r=0.97, p<1e-6 across 11 task types / 245 episodes) [A: plan-012-full, 245eps/11tasks]. Non-death performance is approximately equal between modalities.
- **Supporting finding**: Keyword heuristics structurally fail (match rates degenerate to ≈always-det or ≈always-internal); episode-level counterfactual labels can train a lightweight router (internal_recall=51.5%).
- **Implication**: The value of deterministic computation in interactive environments is concentrated in catastrophic failure prevention, not positive task guidance.

---

## Section Structure

### 1. Introduction (0.8 pages)

**Key points:**
- LLM agents on rule-governed environments (physics, chemistry) suffer catastrophic failures from hallucinated state transitions → motivate the routing question
- Existing work: tool-use learning (Toolformer, ART, Chameleon) learns *when* to invoke tools but doesn't analyze *what* routing learns; ITP-R routes to approximate world models but underperforms pure internal reasoning; ReTool/AgentMath use implicit routing entangled with backbone
- Per-step oracle labeling degenerates in sparse-reward environments (98% tie rate) → need episode-level analysis
- **Contributions** (bulleted):
  1. Episode-level counterfactual methodology that overcomes per-step oracle degeneracy
  2. Empirical finding: death avoidance accounts for ≥90% of routing signal on ScienceWorld (11 tasks, 245 episodes) [A: plan-012-full, 245eps/11tasks]
  3. Structural failure analysis of keyword heuristics; demonstration that counterfactual labels can train a lightweight diagnostic router

### 2. Method (1.0 pages)

**Key points:**
- **2.1 Problem Setup**: ScienceWorld environment; two computation modalities (internal LLM reasoning vs. deterministic simulation via environment forking); per-step routing decision
- **2.2 Episode-Level Counterfactual Labeling**: Why per-step oracle fails (98% tie rate in sparse rewards) → run complete episodes under pure-internal and pure-deterministic strategies → compare episode-level scores → label: det-preferred / internal-preferred / no-preference. Distribution: 86 det-pref / 9 int-pref / 150 no-pref (245 episodes) [A: plan-012-full, 245eps/11tasks]
- **2.3 Death Decomposition Framework**: Decompose Δ_full into death-avoidance component (Δ_death) and non-death component (Δ_nd). Death avoidance fraction = (Δ_full - Δ_nd) / Δ_full. Cross-task correlation: Pearson r between per-task death rate difference and Δ_full

### 3. Experiments (1.5 pages)

**Key points:**
- **3.1 Setup**: Qwen3-1.7B backbone; ScienceWorld 11 task types × 20-40 episodes; evaluation: always-internal, always-deterministic, oracle, random, keyword heuristic, learned router
- **3.2 Death Decomposition Results** (core result):
  - Δ_full=+29.60, Δ_nd=+2.84, death fraction=90.41% [A: plan-012-full, 245eps/11tasks]
  - 10/11 death-prone tasks: death-dominated gaps
  - 1 exception: find-non-living-thing (n=40, 0 deaths, Δ=+9.58 from non-death mechanisms) [A: plan-012-full, 245eps/11tasks]
  - Pearson r=0.9698 (p=8.12e-07) [A: plan-012-full, 245eps/11tasks]
- **3.3 Baseline Comparison**:
  - always-internal: -39.07, always-det: -9.47, oracle: -6.58, random: -22.38 [A: plan-003-baseline-245eps]
  - Keyword heuristic: structural failure (v1 85.8% match → ≈always-det; v2 4.9% → ≈always-internal)
  - Learned router (ablation-b): internal_recall=51.5%, first non-degenerate; classification head variants all degenerate
- **3.4 Analysis**: Death rate: internal 42.9% vs. deterministic 16.3%; alive-episode scores nearly equal across modalities [A: plan-012-full, 245eps/11tasks]

### 4. Related Work (0.5 pages, integrated or separate)

**Key points:**
- **Tool-use learning**: Toolformer (self-supervised API insertion), ART (LLM-as-router), Chameleon (LLM-as-planner), ToolkenGPT (token-level triggers). Differentiation: episode-level counterfactual labeling, safety-aware framing, explicit modular router
- **Adaptive computation / routing**: CogRouter (RL-based), ARES, Mixture-of-Depths. Our focus: empirical analysis of *what* routing learns, not a new routing architecture
- **World model routing**: ITP-R, Dyna-Think. Our deterministic computation is exact (simulator), not approximate (LLM world model)
- **Agent frameworks**: ReAct, Reflexion. Orthogonal — we analyze the routing decision within an agent loop

### 5. Conclusion (0.3 pages)

**Key points:**
- Summary: death avoidance ≥90% of routing signal; episode-level counterfactual analysis as diagnostic methodology
- **Limitations**: single benchmark (ScienceWorld), episode-level granularity (not step-level), DAgger distribution shift (train on pure strategies, deploy on mixed)
- **Future work**: step-level labeling with denser reward signals, extension to MATH/code interpretation domains, DAgger-style iterative relabeling

Our work differs along three axes: (1) we generate routing labels via \emph{episode-level counterfactual analysis}---running complete trajectories under competing strategies---rather than self-supervised or RL-based signals; (2) we frame routing as \emph{catastrophic failure prevention} rather than general tool selection; and (3) we train an explicit lightweight router decoupled from the backbone LLM, enabling diagnostic analysis of what the routing signal encodes.

\paragraph{Adaptive Computation.}
Several recent methods adapt reasoning effort per step.
CogRouter \cite{cogrouter-2026} achieves 82.3\% on ScienceWorld by routing among cognitive depth levels (instinct to strategic planning) via Cooperative Policy Optimization, while ARES \cite{ares-2026} trains a lightweight router to select per-step reasoning effort (low/medium/high), reducing token cost by 52.7\%.
Mixture-of-Recursions \cite{mixture-of-recursions-2025} applies adaptive depth at the architecture level via per-token recursive routing.
These methods route \emph{how much} to reason; we route \emph{which modality} to use (internal LLM reasoning vs.\ deterministic computation) and contribute the empirical finding that death avoidance accounts for ${\sim}99\%$ of the learned routing signal.

\paragraph{World Model Routing.}
ITP \cite{itp-2026} augments agents with LLM-based world model lookahead, adaptively adjusting the simulation horizon based on task progress.
Dyna-Think \cite{dynathink-2025} integrates world model simulation into the reasoning loop, matching 685B-parameter performance with a 32B model at half the token cost.
Both route to \emph{approximate} world models that inherit LLM hallucination failures.
Our deterministic computation modality provides \emph{exact} state transitions, and our counterfactual analysis reveals that this exactness matters almost exclusively for death avoidance---non-death performance is near-equivalent between modalities.

\paragraph{Agent Frameworks.}
ReAct \cite{react-2023} interleaves reasoning and acting in a single LLM call and serves as a foundational framework for interactive agents including our internal-reasoning baseline.
Our work complements ReAct by analyzing \emph{when} reasoning should yield to deterministic computation and finding that the answer is concentrated in catastrophic failure scenarios.
